# The go command compiles a position-independent executable with -shared. It is the
# default build mode on darwin, ios, android and windows, where the nested simd build
# is one too, so a default build is rewritten there. Asking for one where it is not
# the default (-buildmode=pie on linux) still leaves the package alone: the nested
# build would not match it.

# Reference: the scalar program.
exec go run .
cmp stdout want.out

env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG=$WORK/log
env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_LOG_PKGS=example.com/app/vec

[GOOS:darwin] exec go build -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
[GOOS:darwin] cmp log rewrote.want

[GOOS:linux] env LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC_DEBUG=1
[GOOS:linux] exec go build -buildmode=pie -toolexec=$LOOPVEC_TOOLEXEC -o app .
[GOOS:linux] cmp log skipped.want

[GOOS:darwin] exec ./app
[GOOS:darwin] cmp stdout want.out
[GOOS:linux] exec ./app
[GOOS:linux] cmp stdout want.out

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27.1
-- vec/vec.go --
package vec

func AddInt32s(dst, a, b []int32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = a[i] + b[i]
	}
}
-- main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/vec"
)

func main() {
	dst := make([]int32, 21)
	a := make([]int32, 21)
	b := make([]int32, 21)
	for i := range a {
		a[i], b[i] = int32(i), int32(2*i)
	}
	vec.AddInt32s(dst, a, b)
	fmt.Println(dst)
}
-- want.out --
[0 3 6 9 12 15 18 21 24 27 30 33 36 39 42 45 48 51 54 57 60]
-- rewrote.want --
rewrote 1 loop(s) in example.com/app/vec
-- skipped.want --
skipped example.com/app/vec: simd unavailable or unsupported build mode
